title: A Sweep Across a Boolean Buffer
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $y,x$ be Boolean words, let $bits$ be a selector-bit assignment for $M$, let $P$ be a valid input-head position for $y$, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let $\tau_O$ be an integer-indexed Boolean buffer with head position $z_O$. For all $i,j\in\mathbb{N}$ and all Boolean words $rest$, starting the simulator in its decode state with $C$ buffer containing $i$ true bits followed by $j$ false bits and then $rest$, with its head at position $i$, after $j$ steps the $C$ buffer contains $i+j$ true bits followed by $rest$ and its head is at position $i+j$; all the other listed configuration data are unchanged.
caveat: The conclusion is stated using the simulator's decode state and configuration constructor, which are not fully described by the supplied informal definitions.
